title: Scheduler: per-class token budget guardrails to limit tail amplification
author: Marcus Reed
description: Context: With the two-queue (short/long) prototype enabled under mixed prompt-length distributions, we can still see tail amplification when a single scheduling iteration admits too much work from one class (most commonly long-context prefill) and pushes out latency-sensitive short requests. This PR adds per-iteration token budgets per class (and per phase where available) as a guardrail to cap how much token work each class can contribute to a single dispatch/iteration. Once a budget is exhausted we stop admitting additional requests from that class for the current iteration and continue to consider other classes, while preserving existing aging/starvation rules across iterations. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce a budgeted admission step in the scheduler that tracks tokens admitted per class per iteration, (2) add config knobs with safe bounds + defaults appropriate for the prototype, (3) add counters and debug logs for budget overruns so we can see when/why we’re capping, and (4) unit/regression tests covering enforcement and ensuring we don’t deadlock/skip progress. Notes: This is intended as a prototype guardrail, not a full fairness model; we’ll tune defaults via benchmark-lab + perf-canary and keep it behind the mixed-workload scheduler feature flag. Follow-ups: likely split decode vs prefill budgets more cleanly once the prefill/decode separation hooks (PR #24857) are fully rolled out across all runtimes, and add Grafana panels for budget-overrun rates per pool/SKU.
commits: scheduler: add IterationBudget accounting and enforcement hooks
runtime-config: wire scheduler.class_token_budget.* knobs with validation
metrics: add scheduler_token_budget_overrun_total + per-iter admitted tokens
logging: debug-only budget overrun logs (rate-limited) with class/phase context
tests: budget enforcement + regression for mixed workload queue selection
config_knobs_added: scheduler.class_token_budget.enabled (bool, default: false; gated by mixed scheduler flag)
ci_notes: Initial run failed clang-format due to a generated config schema file; fixed by excluding generated output and re-running format.
Bench smoke is non-blocking but was run manually to sanity check no throughput cliff under homogeneous short traffic.
review_conversation: Lena Fischer: The approach makes sense as a guardrail, but I’m worried about default values being too aggressive on A100/H100. Can we (a) cap only long-prefill first, and (b) make the default disabled unless mixed scheduler flag is on? Also naming: ‘token_budget’ vs ‘tokens_per_iter’.

Marcus Reed (author): Updated defaults to be conservative and wired enablement under the mixed scheduler flag only. Renamed internal struct fields to tokens_per_iter for clarity, kept config prefix as class_token_budget.* to group related knobs.

Omar El-Sayed: Please confirm the token accounting aligns with how we estimate prefill cost vs actual tokens admitted (KV cache path has some surprises). If we undercount, budgets won’t help; if we overcount we might throttle unnecessarily.

Marcus Reed (author): We’re using the same token estimate we already pass into batch builder (prompt_tokens for prefill, max_new_tokens for decode admission). Added reason=estimate_mismatch when we observe actual>estimated beyond max_overrun_pct, plus a debug gauge for remaining budget to help validate in canary.

Julian Moore: Metric label cardinality: avoid putting pool/model IDs on overrun counters; keep it class/phase/reason only. Also can we add a counter for ‘iterations capped’ so alerts can be on rate rather than raw overruns.
Marcus Reed (author): Agreed. Labels are limited to class/phase/reason; pool/model attribution comes from existing runtime labels. Added budget_capped_iterations_total for alerting.
Allison Grant: Please add short doc strings for metrics so dashboard work isn’t guessing semantics. Also ensure we don’t emit the gauge in prod by default.
Marcus Reed (author): Added metric docs to runtime-metrics.md and made the gauge debug-only (requires runtime.debug_metrics=true).
Sean Gallagher: Logging: budget overrun logs need to be rate-limited and behind debug; otherwise canary will spam and impact p95 itself.
Marcus Reed (author): Logs are debug level, opt-in via scheduler.class_token_budget.debug_logs=true, and rate-limited via token bucket (default 1 QPS).
testing: Unit: scheduler_budget_guardrails_test covers (1) short class still makes progress when long exhausts budget, (2) long class still makes progress across iterations via existing aging, (3) max_overrun_pct behavior, (4) disabled path is a no-op.
Local load test: replayed synthetic 80/20 mix for 10 minutes; observed lower variance in short TTFT during long-prefill spikes; no regressions in steady-state throughput beyond noise.
rollout_plan: Ship behind mixed-workload scheduler feature flag; default class_token_budget.enabled=false globally.
Enable in us-east canary Dedicated pool with dashboards for (a) p95 by class, (b) token_budget_overrun_total rate, (c) iterations capped rate, (d) queue time by class.
Rollback: disable class_token_budget.enabled or mixed scheduler flag if p95 drifts beyond SRE guardrails.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: it does not change the aging/starvation policy, only bounds per-iteration admission. It should reduce worst-case tail amplification from long-prefill dominating a single iteration. The next step is tuning per SKU and validating with perf-canary once mixed workload scenarios land broadly.
related_prs: PR #24905 (fix long queue starvation edge case) [follow-up]
